small_t_bound: split r into (0,t),(t,1),(1,infinity); removable cancellation gives O(1) on the first piece, the middle is O(1+|log t|), and exponential tails are O(1), hence K_gamma(t)=O(t^-1/2(1+|log t|))
large_t_bound: on (0,1) the removable quotient is uniformly bounded for t>=1; on (1,infinity) both exponentials are dominated by exp(-r/4), hence K_gamma(t)=O(t^-1/2)
laplace: these bounds make integral_0^infinity exp(-xt)K_gamma(t)dt absolutely and locally uniformly convergent for Re x>0
common_domain: therefore gamma causes no restriction beyond the endpoint boundary Re x>1/4
acceptance_test: Jointly audit the split bounds against the source gamma-kernel derivation and attach the authoritative digamma integral theorem used to identify its Laplace transform.
